close_reason: Acknowledged. FileNodeBackend::query_subtree as a trait method (with default impl) is the seam where a backend with a tree-aware index can outperform the default O(depth) loop. The default-impl error-swallow bug was JMAP-510h.4 (closed in eec6d59) and was an independent correctness fix; the trait-method separation itself is correct and stays.
description:
src/backend.rs:134-194 defines query_subtree as a trait method with a default impl. The handler in src/filenode.rs:938-948 calls a single 'backend.query_subtree(...)' instead of looping query_objects(parentId=...) at the handler level.

This is the right separation: the handler describes WHAT it needs (all descendants up to depth N); the backend chooses HOW to fulfill it. Backends with a closure table, nested sets, or recursive CTE override query_subtree with one SQL query. The default impl falls back to O(depth) round-trips for backends that have not bothered to override.

A future contributor might be tempted to inline the loop into the handler (the default impl already exists, why have the indirection?). Defend the trait method: it is the seam where a backend with a tree-aware index can dramatically outperform the default. Inlining the loop into the handler eliminates that optimization point and is a one-way door.

Separate issue: the default impl swallows errors (JMAP-510h.4) — that is a correctness bug, not a flaw in the trait-method separation. Fix .4 without removing the trait method.
title: Good: separate FileNodeBackend::query_subtree trait method (vs. handler doing recursion)
